config.title: Build chat message delivery ack flow

intro.title: Build chat message delivery ack flow
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a chat message delivery acknowledgment (ack) flow to track when messages are successfully sent. You will learn to use Node.js event emitters to simulate sending a message and receiving a confirmation. The core programming concept involves handling asynchronous events and callbacks to manage message states. You will work with JavaScript objects, event listeners, and simple state management. By the end, you'll have a basic system that logs when a message is delivered and acknowledged.
intro.usecase: Message delivery acknowledgments are essential in real-time communication applications like Slack, WhatsApp, and Discord, where users need visual confirmation that their messages have been successfully sent and received. In customer support dashboards, delivery receipts ensure agents know when important updates reach clients, preventing miscommunication. This pattern also appears in collaborative editing tools like Google Docs, where change notifications require confirmation to maintain data consistency across users. Implementing reliable ack flows is crucial for building trustworthy messaging systems that users depend on daily.

objectives: Initialize a message state array to track sent messages and their delivery statuses.
Construct a function to send a new message and assign it a unique identifier and pending status.
Implement a simulated acknowledgment handler that updates a specific message's status to 'delivered'.
Integrate the send function with a user input event to trigger message creation.
Configure a display component to render the list of messages with their current delivery status.
Manipulate the state array by filtering or mapping to show only delivered messages in a separate view.
Bind the acknowledgment handler to a timer or event to simulate server response and update the UI.

steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: Import the EventEmitter class from the 'events' module and the readline module using the require() function.
steps.hint: Use require('events') and require('readline') to import the modules. Remember to destructure EventEmitter from the events module.
steps.seedCode: // Import EventEmitter from 'events' and readline module
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have the EventEmitter class and readline module available for building the chat acknowledgment flow.
successCriteria: EventEmitter is imported from 'events' and readline is imported as a module.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both EventEmitter from 'events' and the readline module using require().
steps.feedbackWrong: import EventEmitter from the 'events' module and the readline module using require().

steps.title: Create the ChatServer class
steps.instruction: Create a ChatServer class that extends EventEmitter. Define it with a constructor that calls super().
steps.hint: Use the class syntax with extends EventEmitter. The constructor should call super() to initialize the EventEmitter parent.
steps.seedCode:
// Import EventEmitter from 'events' and readline module

// Create the ChatServer class
steps.expectedOutcome: A ChatServer class is defined that extends EventEmitter, with a constructor that calls super().
successCriteria: ChatServer class is created, extends EventEmitter, and has a constructor with super() call.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your ChatServer class extends EventEmitter and has a constructor that calls super().
steps.feedbackWrong: The ChatServer class wasn't created correctly. It should extend EventEmitter and have a constructor with super().

steps.title: Initialize message storage in constructor
steps.instruction: Inside the ChatServer class constructor, initialize two properties: an empty array named 'messages' and an empty object named 'pendingAcks'.
steps.hint: Use 'this.messages = []' and 'this.pendingAcks = {}' inside the constructor body.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChatServer constructor now has two initialized properties: messages array and pendingAcks object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've initialized both 'messages' as an empty array and 'pendingAcks' as an empty object inside the constructor.
steps.feedbackWrong: The constructor should initialize both 'messages' and 'pendingAcks' properties. Check the syntax and placement.

steps.title: Create sendMessage method
steps.instruction: Inside the ChatServer class, create a method named sendMessage that takes a sender and content as parameters.
steps.hint: Add a method definition inside the class body. It should look like: sendMessage(sender, content) { }
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChatServer class will have a sendMessage method defined with two parameters.
successCriteria: The sendMessage method is defined inside the ChatServer class with parameters for sender and content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but make sure it's named exactly 'sendMessage' and takes two parameters: sender and content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sendMessage method isn't defined correctly. Check that it's inside the ChatServer class and has the right name and parameters.

steps.title: Create acknowledgeMessage method
steps.instruction: Inside the ChatServer class, add a method named acknowledgeMessage that takes a messageId parameter. The method should update the message's status to 'delivered' and emit an 'acknowledged' event with the messageId.
steps.hint: Remember to access the messages storage and update the status property of the message with the given ID.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChatServer class now has an acknowledgeMessage method that updates message status and emits an event.
successCriteria: The acknowledgeMessage method is defined in the ChatServer class, updates the message status to 'delivered', and emits an 'acknowledged' event with the messageId.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the acknowledgeMessage method, but it might be missing either the status update or the event emission. Check that both actions are included.
steps.feedbackWrong: The acknowledgeMessage method is not correctly implemented. Make sure it updates the message status to 'delivered' and emits an 'acknowledged' event.

steps.title: Set up the chat server instance
steps.instruction: Create an instance of ChatServer and store it in a variable named chatServer.
steps.hint: Use the 'new' keyword followed by the class name to instantiate the ChatServer class.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating an instance of a class
const myServer = new ChatServer();
steps.expectedOutcome: A ChatServer instance is created and assigned to a variable named chatServer.
successCriteria: The chatServer variable is declared and initialized with a new ChatServer instance.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the 'new' keyword and assigning the instance to a variable named chatServer.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to create an instance of the ChatServer class using the 'new' keyword and store it in a variable named chatServer.

steps.title: Initialize the readline interface
steps.instruction: Initialize a readline interface using the readline module you imported, and display a welcome message to the console.
steps.hint: Use the readline.createInterface method to create an interface for terminal input/output, then call console.log to show a welcome message.
steps.expectedOutcome: A readline interface is created and a welcome message appears in the terminal when the code runs.
successCriteria: The readline interface is initialized with process.stdin and process.stdout, and a console.log statement displays a welcome message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've created the readline interface with both input and output streams, and displayed a welcome message using console.log.
steps.feedbackWrong: The readline interface wasn't properly initialized or no welcome message was displayed. Check that you're using readline.createInterface with the correct parameters and calling console.log.

steps.title: Create the handleUserInput function
steps.instruction: Create a function named handleUserInput that takes user input as a parameter and parses commands to route to appropriate chat server actions.
steps.hint: The function should check if the input starts with specific command keywords like 'send', 'ack', or 'pending' and call the corresponding methods on the chat server instance.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleUserInput function is created that can parse user commands and route them to appropriate chat server methods.
successCriteria: The handleUserInput function exists, takes an input parameter, and contains conditional logic to check for command patterns.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it takes an input parameter and contains logic to check for different command patterns.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleUserInput function is missing or doesn't properly parse commands. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Implement send command handling
steps.instruction: Inside the handleUserInput function, add an if statement that checks if the user input starts with 'send ' and calls the chat server's sendMessage method with a unique message ID and the message content.
steps.hint: You can use input.startsWith('send ') to check the command. Generate a unique ID using Date.now().toString() and extract the message content by slicing the input string after 'send '.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleUserInput function will now recognize 'send' commands and create new messages in the chat server.
successCriteria: The handleUserInput function contains an if statement that checks for 'send ' prefix, generates a message ID, extracts content, and calls sendMessage.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your if statement checks for 'send ' exactly and calls sendMessage with both a message ID and the content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The send command handling isn't implemented yet. Add an if statement that processes inputs starting with 'send '.

steps.title: Implement ack command handling
steps.instruction: Add logic to the handleUserInput function that processes 'ack' commands and calls acknowledgeMessage on the chat server instance.
steps.hint: Check if the input starts with 'ack ' and extract the message ID, then call chatServer.acknowledgeMessage with that ID.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleUserInput function will now recognize 'ack' commands and call acknowledgeMessage on the chat server.
successCriteria: The handleUserInput function includes an if statement that checks for 'ack ' prefix, extracts the message ID, and calls chatServer.acknowledgeMessage with that ID.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some logic for the 'ack' command, but it might be incomplete. Make sure to check for the 'ack ' prefix and call acknowledgeMessage with the extracted message ID.
steps.feedbackWrong: The 'ack' command handling is missing or incorrect. The handleUserInput function should process commands starting with 'ack ' and call acknowledgeMessage on the chat server.

steps.title: Wire up the readline interface and start the chat
steps.instruction: Set the readline interface to use the handleUserInput function and display initial instructions to start the interactive chat.
steps.hint: Use the rl.on() method to listen for 'line' events and call handleUserInput with the input. Then display a welcome message using rl.setPrompt() and rl.prompt().
steps.expectedOutcome: The chat application will start and wait for user input, with a prompt showing initial instructions.
successCriteria: The readline interface is set to call handleUserInput on each line of input, and a welcome prompt is displayed.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've both set up the event listener for 'line' events and displayed the initial prompt to start the chat.
steps.feedbackWrong: The readline interface isn't properly connected. Ensure you use rl.on('line', handleUserInput) to handle input and rl.setPrompt() with rl.prompt() to show the initial instructions.
